focus: Advisor and deep-loop suites: whether their cost is config, serialization, install, or duplicated runs
noveltyJustification: All 7 findings were new: corrected census, advisor serial default suite, disjoint stress partition, three suites run twice, serial list at 7 percent, duplicate contract-drift guard, and install-before-test in both workflows.
keyQuestions: Which tests under .skilled/skills/*/runtime are redundant, mirror the implementation, or re-assert the framework, and what does each suite cost on the commit and push path?
Which test infrastructure (custom harnesses, serial lists, shared fixtures, helper layers) costs run time or maintenance without proportional coverage?
ruledOut: Deleting the deep-loop serial list as overengineering
Treating the advisor two suites as a duplicate run

graphEvents.label: Where the advisor and deep-loop suite cost sits
Advisor default suite runs serially with no rationale comment
Three advisor suites run twice per push across two workflows

label: Corrected census: advisor 185 files/35199 lines, deep-loop 174 files/86618 lines; an unpruned find reports 381 and 370
Advisor default suite sets fileParallelism false with no adjacent rationale, serializing the whole default set
Advisor stress and default configs partition files rather than stack, so running both in one job is coverage not duplication
Three advisor suites run twice per push: routing-golden-prompts and two parity ratchets are named in routing-registry-drift and also collected by the stress workflow default run
Deep-loop serial list selects 12 of 173 test files, so only 7 percent of the suite is serialized
deep-loop-runtime.yml re-runs the compiled-contract drift check the commit hook already runs at 0.09s measured
Both slow workflows install and build before the first test, so the suite is the payload and the install is the toll
